newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman issues 97 budget with spending, revenue up.
newsitem.headline: Oman issues 97 budget with spending, revenue up.

text.p: Oman's Sultan Qaboos bin Said issued on Wednesday a decree approving the oil producer's 1997 budget which forecast a substantially higher deficit than previously predicted.
The budget sees higher revenue of 2.003 billion rials ($5.31 billion) and increased spending of 2.266 billion rials.
The estimated deficit of 263 million rials is higher than the 147 million rial deficit Oman predicted for 1997 when it detailed projections for its 1996-2000 five-year plan one year ago.
Economy Minister Ahmad bin Abdul-Nabi Mekki said in a statement that oil income was expected to account for 1.502 billion rials, gas revenue for 69 million and other income for 432 million rials.
Mekki's statement said the revenue calculations for the five-year plan to 2000 were based on an oil price of $15 per barrel.
"Oil prices in 1996 hovered around the $20 per barrel level which is over the price estimate of $15 per barrel for the current five-year plan," Mekki said.

"But in view of the decision to transfer all additional revenue resulting from the improvement in oil prices to the general reserves fund in order to replenish its reserves, the government will continue to implement its policy of controlling expenditures," he said.
Oman's oil output of 900,000 barrels per day (bpd) provides about 75 percent of annual state revenue.
The 1996 budget foresaw total revenue of 1.93 billion rials.
Mekki said the 2.266 billion rials in spending, up from 2.236 in 1996, included 1.815 billion rials in current expenditures and 398 million rials for investments.

Oman, which has said it aims to balance its budget by 2000, had projected a deficit of 218 million rials in 1996. It has said the provisional deficit in 1995 was 274.3 million rials, down from 495.5 million rials in 1994.

Oman's five-year plan -- which predicted the lower 1997 deficit figure of 147 million -- was based on estimated annual expenditure at around 2.1 billion rials. Revenue was expected to rise to 2.12 billion rials in 2000.
Based on these revenue and spending projections, the plan had projected the state deficit to drop to 86 million in 1998 and 87 million in 1999 before being wiped out in the final year of the plan.
